clue.text: Paraded with duke beside river

parts.note: the Aire is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: An aristocrat walks in procession along a riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: Something aired has been shown off publicly, just as a thing paraded is displayed for all to see.

clue.text: Even the sides of a cube are

definitions.meaning: level, with neither side ahead, as in a drawn match

definitions.text: the sides of a cube are
definitions.meaning: every face of a cube is a square, so they are each and every one square

explanation.definitionFit: A level score in sport is described as all square, and every face of a cube literally is a square.

clue.text: Muscles directionally limited?

indicators.note: limited means the word directionally is trimmed at both ends, leaving a run from its middle

explanation.surface: A question about muscles that can only move in certain directions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limited' cuts DI from the front and ONALLY from the back of 'directionally', leaving its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Recti are straight muscles, such as the rectus abdominis, so the plural names a group of muscles.

clue.text: Leather suits family members

parts.note: suits in the sense of 'is good enough for', as in 'that does me'
kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: Leather goods are said to be right for every relative.
explanation.definitionFit: Doeskin is soft leather made from the hide of a female deer.

clue.text: Demonstrated to concertmaster material for piano, perhaps

parts.note: to demonstrate by occupying a place is to stage a sit-in, so demonstrated is sat in
Sir Henry Wood was the conductor who founded the London Proms concerts

explanation.surface: Someone shows a violin leader what a piano case can be made of.
explanation.walkthrough: SAT IN is a protest by occupation. Henry Wood, founder of the Proms (London's summer concert season), is the concert master.
explanation.definitionFit: Satinwood is a fine, glossy timber used in cabinet-making, including the casing of pianos.

clue.text: Smart to accept latest odds? Uncertain

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the final odds at the start of a horse race
iffy is informal for doubtful or uncertain

explanation.surface: A gambler hesitates over whether to take the final odds offered.
explanation.walkthrough: The starting price (SP) in horse racing is the last odds offered before the off.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiffy is informal for stylish and neatly dressed, a synonym of smart.

clue.text: Laboratory apparatus in river transport

parts.note: the Test is a river in Hampshire, famous for trout fishing
the Tube is London's underground railway

explanation.surface: Scientific glassware is shipped along a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is the London Underground railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A small glass cylinder closed at one end is a standard piece of laboratory equipment.

clue.text: Piece of cake lacking surface moisture

parts.note: lacking means having no, so it gives no
sweat is the moisture that appears on the skin's surface

explanation.surface: A cake that has dried out on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms for a task that is very easy to do.

clue.text: As a rule, not many people are in it

definitions.text: As a rule, not many people are in it

parts.words: As a rule, not many people are in it
parts.note: read 'as a rule' as 'as a form of rule': a system of government where only a few people hold power

explanation.definitionFit: Government by a small privileged group is literally rule by the few, from Greek for few and rule.

clue.text: Who dealt with this robot?

parts.note: Who is the time-travelling Doctor of the BBC series, who fought these metal-cased machine-like foes

explanation.walkthrough: Doctor Who is a long-running BBC science-fiction series; the capital W hides the hero's name in a question word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Doctor's most famous enemies are mutant creatures in armoured casings, often described as robots.

clue.text: Money legal action got back for philosopher

parts.note: lucre is money, especially gained dishonourably

indicators.note: got back signals that the word for legal action is turned round

parts.note: a suit is a lawsuit

explanation.surface: Someone wins cash back from a lawsuit against a thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucretius was the Roman poet-thinker who wrote De Rerum Natura.

clue.text: Spread piles of pitch

indicators.note: spread here means scattered about, so the letters of piles are rearranged

explanation.surface: Heaps of tar are spread out on a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A salesman's patter or sales talk is called a pitch.

clue.text: Soon into one's stride, living from foreign currency

parts.note: quick is an old word for living, as in 'the quick and the dead'
off means away from, as in 'off the shelf'
the mark was the German currency before the euro

explanation.surface: Someone lives by trading money from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fast to start reacting or acting is the idiom from a runner leaving the starting line.

clue.text: Ahead of time, forest's set on fire

indicators.note: ahead of means the forest's name comes before the time letter

parts.note: the Forest of Arden is the woodland setting of As You Like It

explanation.surface: A woodland is set alight early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' is a link word; 'Ahead of' places ARDEN before T.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent means burning, figuratively passionate, as if aflame.

clue.text: Unload, having ridden bus that's broken down

indicators.note: broken down signals that the letters of ridden bus are rearranged

explanation.surface: A passenger offloads after a bus breaks down.
explanation.definitionFit: To disburden is to relieve of a load, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Scot able to get drunk in bar

indicators.note: to get drunk suggests the letters of Scot able reel about

explanation.surface: A Scotsman manages to get tipsy in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: An obstacle is a barrier, and to bar is to block, so the noun bar fits.

clue.text: Fungus producing heavenly bodies

parts.note: Earth is a planet, a heavenly body
a star is a heavenly body

explanation.surface: A mushroom that gives rise to planets and stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthstars are fungi whose outer skin splits into a star shape on the ground.

clue.text: Such a reaction could make Grace ill

definitions.note: the definition is a noun phrase, the answer the adjective that describes that kind of reaction

indicators.note: could make signals that Grace ill is reworked into another word

explanation.surface: A bodily reaction could leave a woman called Grace unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypersensitive immune response to a substance is the kind of reaction the adjective names.

clue.text: Collection of clothes for ballet dancers

definitions.meaning: an outfit of garments worn together
a group of performers, such as a corps de ballet

explanation.surface: A wardrobe set aside for performers.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a coordinated outfit and a body of performers working together.

clue.text: Achieve progress in a garden suburb in late spring

indicators.note: the second in places the letter and the suburb inside the month

parts.note: May is a month in late spring
Kew is a London suburb, home to the Royal Botanic Gardens

explanation.surface: A gardener makes headway in a leafy suburb late in the spring.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' is only a link word; 'Achieve progress' reads as surface but is the definition, the nautical sense of moving ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: To make way is to move forward, especially of a ship advancing.

clue.text: For example, collect rand held by settler

definitions.note: a collect is a short prayer in Anglican and Catholic worship, so it is an example of the answer

indicators.note: held by places the currency letter inside the word for settler

parts.note: someone who settles a bill is a payer
R is the abbreviation for the South African rand

explanation.surface: A colonist pockets South African money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collect' (stress on the first syllable) is a short liturgical prayer, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A collect is a brief set prayer read in church services.

clue.text: Revolutionary Chinese character

definitions.meaning: a component of a Chinese written character, used to index it in dictionaries

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an extremist reformer and the indexing element of a written Chinese symbol.

clue.text: Sort of cake offered as incentive

definitions.meaning: a sponge cake made with a grated root vegetable
an inducement, as in the dangled reward for a donkey

explanation.definitionFit: It names both a familiar root-vegetable cake and a reward dangled to motivate.

clue.text: Joint eaten with bread and punch

parts.note: a knuckle is a finger joint
a sandwich is a filling eaten with bread

explanation.surface: A cut of meat served between slices of bread with a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punch' looks like the drink to go with the meal; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a blow to the mouth with the fist.

clue.text: They can't take off in Wellington, say

definitions.text: They can't take off in Wellington, say

parts.words: They can't take off in Wellington, say
parts.note: describes flightless birds, and also the nickname for people from New Zealand, whose capital is Wellington

explanation.walkthrough: Wellington is New Zealand's capital, not the boot.
explanation.definitionFit: The flightless national bird of New Zealand gives its nickname to New Zealanders.

clue.text: Northerner joining one special unit

definitions.note: the people's name is used here for a single member

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: special suggests an unusual arrangement of the letters of unit

explanation.surface: A man from the north signs up to an elite military squad.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inuit are the indigenous peoples of the Arctic, the far north.

clue.text: Character merry as result of champagne?

definitions.text: Character merry as result of champagne?

parts.words: Character merry as result of champagne?
parts.note: points to the title role of Lehar's operetta The Merry ... and to Veuve Clicquot, champagne named after a bereaved wife

explanation.walkthrough: Veuve, in Veuve Clicquot champagne, is French for a woman whose husband has died.
explanation.definitionFit: The Merry Widow is the operetta heroine, and the Clicquot widow gave her name to champagne.

clue.text: Artist redesigned graticule

indicators.note: redesigned signals that the letters of graticule are laid out afresh

explanation.surface: A painter reworks a grid of lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Theodore Gericault was the French Romantic painter of The Raft of the Medusa.

clue.text: Craft relying on onshore winds

parts.note: a sailing vehicle that runs over beaches rather than water, powered by wind on land

explanation.definitionFit: A wheeled sail-powered vehicle raced on beaches, driven by the wind over the shore.

clue.text: King and others returned? Not yet

indicators.note: returned signals that the king and the others are read backwards together

parts.note: R is short for Rex, Latin for king
et al is Latin shorthand for and others

explanation.surface: A monarch and his entourage have come back.
explanation.definitionFit: Later means at a future time, so something happening then has not happened yet.
